q_legs8.question: Does it have 8 legs?
q_legs8.hint: Spiders and their cousins have 8 legs and no antennae.

q_pincers.question: Does it have pincers and a tail with a stinger?
q_pincers.hint: Look at the front and at the tip of the back end.

q_many.question: Does it have lots and lots of legs, more than 20?
q_many.hint: If it has about 14 legs and rolls into a ball, it's something else.

q_long_legs.question: Are its legs long and sticking out to the sides?
q_long_legs.hint: A centipede has one pair of long legs per ring; a millipede has two short pairs underneath.

q_wings.question: Does it have wings?
q_wings.hint: Careful: sometimes the wings are folded under a hard cover.

q_waist.question: Does it have a very thin waist between the thorax and the abdomen?

q_scales.question: Does it have big, colorful, dusty wings?
q_scales.hint: That dust is made of tiny scales.

q_club.question: Do its antennae end in a little knob?
q_club.hint: Butterflies have knobbed antennae; moths have thread-like or feathery ones.

q_elytra.question: Is its back covered by two hard wings that meet in a straight line?
q_elytra.hint: Those hard covers are called elytra: beetles have them.

q_dots.question: Is it small, round and spotted?

q_light.question: Does it have little lights on its body?
q_light.hint: Some beetles carry their own lanterns.

q_jump.question: Are its back legs very big, for jumping?

q_pray.question: Are its front legs folded, as if it were praying?

q_two.question: Does it have just two wings, one on each side?
q_two.hint: Bees have four, but the ones on each side are hooked together and look like two.

q_beak_long.question: Does it have very long legs and a long, thin beak?

q_flat.question: Is it flat, with very long antennae?
q_flat.hint: Antennae almost as long as its body.

q_dragon.question: Does it have a very long, stick-like abdomen and huge eyes?

q_waist2.question: Does it have a thin waist between the thorax and the abdomen?
q_waist2.hint: Bees, wasps and ants are in the same family.

q_hairy.question: Is it fuzzy?
q_hairy.hint: Bees are fuzzy, to carry pollen; wasps are smooth and shiny.

q_beak.question: Does it have a sucking beak under its head?
q_beak.hint: Bugs and cicadas suck sap or juices with their beak.

q_clear.question: Are its wings clear and longer than its body?

r_arana.name: a spider
r_arana.fact: Eight legs and no antennae. It's a cousin of insects and a great hunter.

r_alacran.name: a scorpion
r_alacran.fact: An arachnid with pincers and a stinger. Watch from a distance and tell an adult.

r_cochinita.name: a pill bug
r_cochinita.fact: A cousin of shrimp! It has 14 legs and rolls into a ball.

r_ciempies.name: a centipede
r_ciempies.fact: A fast hunter with one pair of legs per ring. Look without touching.

r_milpies.name: a millipede
r_milpies.fact: It moves slowly, eats dead leaves and curls up when scared.

r_hormiga.name: an ant
r_hormiga.fact: Workers have no wings. They live in colonies and work as a team.

r_joven.name: a young insect (nymph or larva)
r_joven.fact: Many young insects don't have wings yet. When they grow up, they may fly.

r_mariposa.name: a butterfly
r_mariposa.fact: Knobbed antennae and scaly wings. It almost always flies by day.

r_polilla.name: a moth
r_polilla.fact: A cousin of the butterfly, with thread-like or feathery antennae. It almost always flies at night.

r_mariquita.name: a ladybug
r_mariquita.fact: A small beetle that eats the aphids on plants.

r_cocuyo.name: a click beetle firefly
r_cocuyo.fact: A Venezuelan beetle with two green lights on its thorax.

r_escarabajo.name: a beetle
r_escarabajo.fact: Hard cover wings: it's in the group with the most species in the world.

r_saltamontes.name: a grasshopper or a cricket
r_saltamontes.fact: Spring-loaded back legs. Crickets sing by rubbing their wings.

r_santateresa.name: a praying mantis
r_santateresa.fact: It hunts with its front legs and turns its head to look at you.

r_zancudo.name: a mosquito
r_zancudo.fact: Two wings and a thin beak. Only females bite.

r_mosca.name: a fly
r_mosca.fact: Two wings and huge eyes. Many flies help with recycling.

r_cucaracha.name: a cockroach
r_cucaracha.fact: Flat to squeeze into cracks. In the forest, it recycles leaves.

r_libelula.name: a dragonfly
r_libelula.fact: Huge eyes and four strong wings. It catches mosquitoes in flight.

r_abeja.name: a bee
r_abeja.fact: Fuzzy so it can carry pollen from flower to flower.

r_avispa.name: a wasp
r_avispa.fact: Smooth, with a thin waist. It hunts caterpillars and other pests.

r_cigarra.name: a cicada
r_cigarra.fact: Glass-like wings and a very loud song on hot days.

r_chinche.name: a true bug
r_chinche.fact: It sucks juices with its beak. Look without touching, in case it's a kissing bug.

r_otro.name: an insect this key doesn't know yet
r_otro.fact: There are over a million kinds of insects! Draw it in your notebook and ask your teacher.
